Independent corroboration from AWS CloudTrail (cross-source log audit, 2026-07-30). These are server-side records of the `bedrock:Converse` calls themselves, so they confirm the error text and exact timing independently of anything we logged locally.

Every `Converse` call in the account in July occurred today; 14 of 31 carried an errorCode. The 11 `ValidationException`s were all made under `user/joe_frontier`:

    2026-07-30T16:03:39Z  Invocation of model ID anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 with on-demand
                          throughput isn't supported. Retry your request with the ID or ARN
                          of an inference profile.
    2026-07-30T20:34:19Z  The model returned the following errors: `temperature` is deprecated for this model.
    2026-07-30T20:34:21Z  The model returned the following errors: `temperature` is deprecated for this model.
    2026-07-30T20:34:23Z  The provided model identifier is invalid.        (x4 in the same second)
    2026-07-30T20:34:23Z  The model returned the following errors: `temperature` is deprecated for this model.
    2026-07-30T20:35:01Z  The model returned the following errors: `temperature` is deprecated for this model.
    2026-07-30T20:35:01Z  The model returned the following errors: `temperature` is deprecated for this model.
    2026-07-30T20:35:04Z  The model returned the following errors: `top_p` is deprecated for this model.

Two things this adds beyond what the ticket already records:

1. The `top_p` variant is confirmed as a real server-side rejection (a single occurrence, 20:35:04Z), not merely inferred from the `temperature` case. Both parameters are rejected by the same class of model.
2. `The provided model identifier is invalid` fired 4x within one second at 20:34:23Z, interleaved with the `temperature` rejections. That is a distinct failure from the deprecation errors and may indicate the override-table miss and an id-resolution miss are being hit on the same code path. Worth confirming they are two bugs, not one, before scoping the fix. (Possibly relevant to 281f, where `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` is parsed but read by nothing.)

Separately, and NOT part of this bug: the same CloudTrail sweep shows 3x `AccessDenied` on `bedrock:Converse` at 16:59:59Z, 17:01:28Z and 17:02:09Z under `arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/i-00880b2c7f13527c5` — the production box. That belongs to story 9249 (grant the review-bot Bedrock access), noted here only so the two are not conflated when reading the timeline.

Method: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Converse` over 2026-07-01 -> 07-30, us-east-1.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
SCOPE EXTENDED — the same defect is live on the DIRECT-ANTHROPIC path, confirmed by a production
observation, not only on Bedrock.

OPERATOR REPORT: the code-review bot logs "Sampling parameters ['temperature'] are not supported by
'claude-opus-4-8'" on essentially every call.

VERIFIED, three ways:
1. `capabilities_for("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8").supports_temperature` was TRUE — the override table
   covered only the Bedrock-prefixed ids, so rebar kept SENDING temperature on the Anthropic path.
2. That log line is emitted verbatim by pydantic-ai at models/anthropic.py:641, from
   `_drop_unsupported_sampling_settings`.
3. `models/bedrock.py` contains ZERO occurrences of that helper. So it is ONE defect with TWO symptoms:
   the Anthropic adapter silently DROPS the parameter and warns; the Bedrock adapter has no such drop
   and the call 400s. The earlier Bedrock-only framing of this ticket was too narrow.

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN LOG NOISE. The warning is the visible half. The real cost is that a pass pinning
temperature=0 for determinism silently does not get it. `workflow/gates/code-review.yaml:155` pins
`temperature: 0` on the Pass-2 verify step, with the stated reason: "Greedy Pass-2 verification:
re-running the same finding must not resample its narrow yes/no verification and drift impact/validity."
And code review has NO verifier downgrade — it never calls `resolve_verifier_model`, so ALL of its
passes (base/round_a/round_b, verify, coach) run on cfg.model = claude-opus-4-8. So code-review's Pass-2
has been resampling in production, which is a plausible source of review nondeterminism. That is a
correctness finding, not a cosmetic one.

FIX: added the BARE ids `claude-opus-4-8` and `claude-opus-4-7` to the override table. The table keys on
the bare id (`_model_id_of` strips the provider prefix), so these cover BOTH `anthropic:<id>` and the
bare string, while the `us.`/`global.` entries continue to cover Bedrock. Withdrawing the parameter is
WIRE-IDENTICAL to having it dropped downstream — the same request goes out either way — but it removes
the per-call warning and, more importantly, removes the false belief that greedy decoding is in effect.

ONE PRE-EXISTING TEST WAS CORRECTED, not weakened. `test_supports_temperature_defaults_true_for_
everything_else` used `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` as its example of an UNLISTED model, asserting it kept
temperature. That exemplar encoded a fact this observation disproves. The test's intent ("the denylist
must not leak") and its assertion count are unchanged; the example moved to models that are genuinely
unlisted and measured to accept temperature (`anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`, `openai:gpt-4o`).

FOLLOW-ON worth its own consideration, NOT done here: rebar sends temperature whenever configured, and
learns it was ignored only from a provider log line. A pass that REQUIRES greedy decoding cannot tell
whether it got it. Consider making `supports_temperature=False` visible where determinism is assumed —
e.g. Pass-2 warning once when it pins temperature=0 on a model whose capability record says the
parameter is withdrawn. That is exactly the "green signal whose measurement could not be verified" shape
epic 3147 exists for.

compiled_state.description:
# The `supports_temperature` override table is incomplete — the default model is unguarded

## Context / Problem

Story 2932 landed a MEASURED override so Bedrock models that reject `temperature` have it withdrawn rather than hard-failing (`src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:95`, consumed at `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:399`). The table has exactly ONE entry:

```python
_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES = {
    "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7": {"supports_temperature": False},
}
```

A fresh measurement sweep shows the behaviour is **family-wide across the opus line and both profile prefixes**, so the single entry leaves rebar's own DEFAULT model unguarded.

## MEASURED — account 896586841071, us-east-1, boto3 `bedrock-runtime.converse`, maxTokens 8

| model id | temp unset | temp=0.0 | temp=0.5 | temp=1.0 | topP=0.9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` | OK | OK | OK | — | — |
| `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` | OK | OK | — | — | — |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` | OK | **400** | **400** | OK | **400** |
| `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` | OK | **400** | — | — | — |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` | OK | **400** | — | — | — |
| `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` | — | **400** | — | — | — |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5` | ValidationException: invalid model identifier | | | | |
| `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5` | ValidationException: invalid model identifier | | | | |

Error text: `ValidationException: \`temperature\` is deprecated for this model.` (and `\`top_p\` is deprecated for this model.`)

## What the data actually says (three corrections to the current model)

1. **`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` is affected, and it is rebar's `DEFAULT_MODEL`** (`config.py:39` = `claude-opus-4-8`). The table does not list it, so the guard does not fire. This is the single most likely Bedrock Pass-1 model — especially under the operator requirement that Pass-1 run opus (see eb6e) — and it would hard-fail the moment any temperature is configured.
2. **The `global.` prefix is affected too.** The table keys on the full model id, so `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` are both unguarded even if the `us.` twins are listed. Any fix keyed literally per-id must cover both prefixes, or be matched on the family portion.
3. **It is NOT 'temperature unsupported' — it is 'explicit non-default sampling rejected'.** `temp=1.0` (the API default) SUCCEEDS on opus-4-8 while 0.0 and 0.5 fail. So the deprecation is of the parameter's *tunability*. `supports_temperature=False` still produces correct behaviour (withdraw the parameter → the model uses its default), but the field NAME misdescribes the mechanism, which matters for the next person extending it.

**`top_p` is deprecated on opus-4-8 as well, and there is no `supports_top_p` on the capability record.** This is currently LATENT, not live: rebar never sets `top_p` anywhere in `src/rebar`. But `failure.py:367` already lists `top_p`/`top_k` as sampling parameters rebar 'can send', so the gap becomes live the day anything sets one.

## Why this matters now

- The Pass-2 verifiers deliberately pin `temperature=0` (`code-review.yaml:155`). That is safe ONLY while Pass-2 stays on sonnet, which accepts it. It is the per-pass model split (eb6e) that keeps this from being an outage.
- The production cutover ships with **no fallback**, so an unguarded 400 here is a stuck gate, not a degraded one.
- `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5` and `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5` are NOT invokable in this account at all — worth noting because an earlier note in this epic recorded cache measurements for opus-4-5, and that model id does not resolve here now. Any conclusion resting on it should be re-measured rather than trusted.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — extend the override table (or match on the family portion of the id so both `us.` and `global.` prefixes are covered by one entry).
- `tests/unit/` — a test per newly-covered id asserting the parameter is withdrawn.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts `capabilities_for("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8").supports_temperature`
      is False. NOTE the PROVIDER-QUALIFIED form: `_model_id_of` returns None for a bare id with no
      colon, so a bare-string assertion passes VACUOUSLY against the conservative record without ever
      exercising the override table. Production always passes `provider:model` or a model object.
- [ ] a test asserts the same for `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and for both `opus-4-7` prefixes
- [ ] a test asserts `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` retains `supports_temperature is True` (the guard must not over-apply and silently drop determinism from the model that supports it)
- [ ] the table's comment records the measured matrix above, including that temp=1.0 succeeds, so the next reader does not re-derive it
compiled_state.title: Bedrock temperature override table misses claude-opus-4-8 (the DEFAULT model) and the global.* variants
